what_happened: On 2026-11-14, with Sri's approval, the person running Athena reordered the queue by hand, outside any job. They set three known fixes to urgent: the misread-field bug, the failing batch-ordering test and the throughput clock. They held three items that loop on the queue because they are budget-short or always refused. They raised 62 steward and Hestia fix requests to high and left website and study content as it was. They also filed three urgent requests: queue out-of-scope follow-ups as requests, rank Athena's own fixes ahead of feature work, and count fixes queued against fixes run. Sri's earlier "fixes first" reset request had been read as one Hestia change. That reading left queue order out of scope, and nothing queued its follow-ups, so Sri chose a one-time manual unblock. The event lists no acceptance criteria, findings or failed checks.
cause: Athena has no rule that ranks its own fixes ahead of feature work, and no way to turn a reading's out-of-scope items into queued requests. A priority reset such as "fixes first" is therefore read as a single change, and queue order is left out. Nothing counts fixes queued against fixes run, so the backlog of fixes grew unnoticed. Only a person could re-rank the queue and hold the looping items. This fits the existing priority-inflation class: tiers are applied freely, 62 requests needed re-tiering, and looping or already-handled items stayed queued until someone noticed.
other_causes: Items that are budget-short or always refused keep looping on the queue because nothing holds or retires them automatically.
The reading of Sri's request had no step that turns its out-of-scope parts into follow-up requests.
open_hypotheses: Whether the 62 requests raised to high were all correctly tiered cannot be told from the fields given.
Whether the three held items were held because they are budget-short or because they are always refused is not stated per item.
contradictions: The event is a one-time manual unblock approved by Sri, not a failed job. The class fits only partly: it describes re-tiering by hand, and this event also covers holding looping items and a reading that dropped queue order.
prevention: Three changes together would prevent the whole class. (1) Rank Athena's own fixes ahead of feature work by default, with tiers capped and reviewed so urgent and high keep meaning. (2) Queue every out-of-scope follow-up from an accepted reading as its own request. (3) Report the count of fixes queued against fixes run, and hold items that loop because they are budget-short or always refused until someone reviews them.
proposed_request: Make Athena's queue rank its own fixes ahead of feature work by default. (a) When a reading marks part of a request as out of scope, queue each such part as a separate request, linked to the original, instead of dropping it. (b) Add a status line that counts fixes queued against fixes run. (c) Hold any queued item that has been refused repeatedly, or whose budget is below the stage caps, and list held items on the status page with the reason. Acceptance: a test queue holding one feature job and one fix job runs the fix first. A reading with an out-of-scope part produces a queued follow-up request. The status output shows both fix counts. A repeatedly refused item is held and not retried. Add a CHANGELOG.md entry.
